page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on 64-bit ARM processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. It does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

A key component of the hardware configuration is the integration of 2832 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. The local NVMe SSD volume provides fast, low-latency scratch space and temporary caching capabilities directly tied to the host machine. Public IPv4 networking requires independent provisioning, as zero complimentary public addresses are packaged with the base instance.

From a cost-efficiency and infrastructure perspective, the ARM64 compute cores deliver dense processing capacity with favorable power-to-performance characteristics compared to traditional architectures. The combination of high core counts, substantial memory capacity, and large local NVMe storage reduces external block-storage bottlenecks for intermediate processing phases, though applications must be compatible with the ARM instruction set architecture.

The D48pds_v7 instance is targeted at enterprise workloads that require balanced computational capacity and direct high-speed local disk I/O. Common target deployments include large-scale web and application servers, containerized microservices clusters, relational database engines using ephemeral cache, software build environments, and data transformation or ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine engineered on the 64-bit ARM processor architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A defining characteristic of this configuration is its integrated 2832 GB local NVMe SSD, which delivers high-speed, low-latency storage for temporary data processing and disk caching, paired with support for Azure Premium Storage. The server does not contain dedicated graphics processing units, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. By combining dense ARM compute cores with extensive local non-volatile storage, the platform offers balanced computational efficiency for multi-threaded systems. The instance is suited for enterprise application hosting, large web server fleets, relational database backends, distributed microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional ETL processing tasks.
